newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian PM expresses "regret" at Belarus crisis.
newsitem.headline: Russian PM expresses "regret" at Belarus crisis.

text.p: Russian Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin expressed "deep regret" on Sunday over the collapse of the compromise he brokered between Belarus's president and parliament and blamed some legislators there for wrecking the truce.

But the Russian premier, who talked through the night with Belarus President Alexander Lukashenko and parliamentary leaders to reach a deal on Friday, told Itar-Tass news agency that Lukashenko could also have done more to make it succeed.

Chernomyrdin said the events leading up to Sunday's controversial referendum on vastly strengthening Lukashenko's powers "provoke great regret and demonstrate that a group of deputies of the Belarus Supreme Soviet lack a basic sense of responsibility for the fate of the country and its people".
"A group of deputies of the Belarus parliament were behind the breakdown of the agreements reached," he went on.
But he added: "The executive branch of power in Belarus failed to show the insistence and endurance needed to bring the agreements into effect."

Lukashenko abandoned the accords on Saturday after parliament failed to muster the required majority to support its part of the agreement, under which impeachment proceedings against Lukashenko were to be dropped in return for a softening of his stance on implementing constitutional change.

Russian President Boris Yeltsin, who claimed on Friday the Moscow-brokered accord was a "great victory" for Russian diplomacy, insisted on Saturday that despite the setback it had nonetheless prepared the way for a defusing of the crisis.
A spokesman for Chernomyrdin told Tass that the prime minister had not spoken to Lukashenko on Sunday and had no plans to do so.
